issues.display_title: Issue #2072: Investigation: suspected orphan Stripe subscription sub_7Sw3dH7VXTLcVP (User 670) — not an orphan, belongs to User 1264
issues.main_description_html:
Origin

Found during the Stripe audit on 2026-10-13. User 670 is still billed $75/month on Stripe,
but the DB shows no active plan. The next renewal is on 2026-10-18. Whether to cancel the
subscription (and refund) or re-link it is a separate PM/Management decision. This issue only
covers finding out why the DB and Stripe got out of sync.

User

  • User ID: 670 (zakkl@rebranding360.com)
  • users.subscribtion = 0
  • user_extra_data.recurring_profile empty, payasyougo empty
  • Stripe subscription: sub_7Sw3dH7VXTLcVP, active, Agency $75/month, created 2015-12-03
  • Last paid invoice: 2026-09-18

Goal

Find the cause of the orphan subscription, and decide whether this only affects User 670 or is
a bug that can create more orphan subscriptions.

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001: The root cause is identified, with evidence (timeline of DB changes vs Stripe events).
  • AC-002: Conclusion on scope: User 670 only, or a code path that can create more orphan
    subscriptions.
  • AC-003: If it's systemic: list the other affected users (active Stripe subscription while
    the DB has no plan) and open a follow-up fix issue.
  • AC-004: Findings written up in docs/investigations/.

Result

Not an orphan. sub_7Sw3dH7VXTLcVP belongs to User 1264 (REbranding360 Inc., subscribtion = 5 Agency Monthly), linked via recurring_profile = cus_7Sw3ZuKbDVElt8. The 2026-10-13 audit matched it to User 670 only by the Stripe customer email (zakkl@rebranding360.com).

  • User 1264's plan matches the subscription price (Agency Monthly, $75/month).
  • All charges are recorded under User 1264: cc_logs_stripe (incl. the 2026-08/09 renewals from the current cron), cc_purchase (from the first charge on 2015-12-03), cc_logs.
  • The profile and history were moved from User 670 to User 1264, very likely on 2016-04-12 (cc_logs rows 399/400 say "for: 670" but carry user_id = 1264).
  • None of the API code paths that clear recurring_profile were involved.

Here the detail: https://github.com/GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New/blob/main/docs/investigations/2026-10-16-user-670-orphan-stripe-subscription.md

Action: no cancel or refund needed. The 2026-10-18 renewal is a legitimate charge for User 1264.

issues.display_title: Issue #2074: feat(feature-flags): API that returns the SSO switch per environment (dev / live)
issues.main_description_html:
Background

The Single Sign-On (SSO) switch added in GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4388 is a dashboard build setting (REACT_APP_KEYCLOAK_AUTH_ENABLED). Turning SSO on or off needs a dashboard rebuild and deploy, and the dev and live dashboards can't be switched separately. That approach is now outdated.

Goal

The API tells the dashboard whether SSO is on. The switch is stored in Redis, so it can be changed without a deploy, separately for dev and live.

Scope

  • GET /v1/feature-flags?env=dev|live: works without login and returns the switch in the standard response format (not encrypted): { "statusCode": 200, "data": { "messages": "...", "env": "dev", "keycloak_auth": true } }
    • Without env, the API answers for live. Any value other than dev or live is rejected (422).
  • The switch is read from Redis (Toronto), with one key per environment:
    • feature_flags:dev:keycloak_auth
    • feature_flags:live:keycloak_auth
    • 1 (or true) means on, 0 means off. To change it, set the value (SET <key> 1 / SET <key> 0); keys are not deleted. A missing key counts as off.
  • There is only one API (production) and one Redis for both dev and live, which is why the dashboard has to say which environment it is.
  • If Redis can't be read, the API returns an error (500). The dashboard then shows an error with a "Try Again" button.
  • Only the SSO switch for now. The response can carry more switches later.

Out of Scope

  • A screen or API for changing the switch (it is set directly in Redis for now).
  • Moving maintenance mode to the API.
  • Dashboard changes (GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4395).

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001: With feature_flags:live:keycloak_auth set to 1, GET /v1/feature-flags returns keycloak_auth: true. With 0 it returns false.
  • AC-002: ?env=dev reads only the dev key. Changing the dev key does not change the live answer, and vice versa.
  • AC-003: A missing key returns keycloak_auth: false.
  • AC-004: An env other than dev or live returns 422.
  • AC-005: The endpoint works without logging in.
  • AC-006: If Redis can't be read, the response is 500 with the standard error body.
  • AC-007: Unit tests cover AC-001 – AC-006.

Setup before release

  • SET feature_flags:dev:keycloak_auth 0
  • SET feature_flags:live:keycloak_auth 0

Related

  • GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4388: SSO switch as a build setting (outdated by this task)
  • GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4395: dashboard reads the switch from this API

Result

Implementation

  • PR: #2075 — merged into main on 2026-10-16 (merge commit d78dd02)
  • Key commit: e5421db — feat(feature-flags): add public GET /v1/feature-flags reading SSO flag from Redis
  • Behavior:
    • GET /v1/feature-flags?env=dev|live works without login and returns { "env": "...", "keycloak_auth": true|false } in the standard response format, not encrypted.
    • The switch is read from Redis per environment: feature_flags:dev:keycloak_auth and feature_flags:live:keycloak_auth. 1 means on, 0 (or a missing key) means off.
    • Without env the API answers for live; any other value is rejected with 422. If Redis can't be read, the response is 500.
  • To turn SSO on or off: SET feature_flags:<dev|live>:keycloak_auth 1 (on) or 0 (off). It takes effect on the dashboard's next page load, no deploy needed.
  • Docs: docs/v2/feature-flags/get-feature-flags.md.

Testing

  • All acceptance criteria (AC-001 – AC-007) verified and passed.
  • Unit tests: tests/DTOs/FeatureFlags, tests/Repositories/FeatureFlags, tests/Actions/FeatureFlags, tests/Http/Controllers/FeatureFlags, tests/Routes/FeatureFlagsRoutesTest.php.
